name: Literature-in-English
topics: Prose: narrative techniques and plot structure
Prose: point of view, characterisation and setting
Unseen prose: an ORIGINAL short extract written into the question
Unseen poetry: ORIGINAL short lines written into the question
Tone, mood, theme and subject matter

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT regarded as one of the three major genres of literature?
questions.e: Poetry, prose and drama are the three major genres of literature. Biography is simply a type of prose writing, not a separate major genre.
questions.p: Poetry, prose and drama na di three main genre of literature. Biography na just one kind prose work, e no be im own major genre.

questions.q: A piece of literature written mainly to be performed before an audience on stage, using dialogue and stage directions, is best classified as a work of...
questions.e: Drama is the genre of literature written for performance, made up of dialogue between characters and stage directions to guide actors.
questions.p: Drama na di genre of literature wey dem write make dem perform am for stage, e get dialogue between characters and stage directions wey dey guide di actors.

questions.q: Read this line: 'The old fisherman's hands were cracked maps of a thousand storms.' Which figure of speech is used here?
questions.e: The fisherman's hands are directly called 'maps' without using 'like' or 'as', so this is a metaphor, a direct comparison between two unlike things.
questions.p: Dem call di fisherman hand 'maps' straight straight, dem no use 'like' or 'as', so na metaphor, na direct comparison between two different things.

questions.q: In drama, what do we call a speech given by a character who is alone on stage, in which he reveals his true inner thoughts and feelings to the audience?
questions.e: A soliloquy is spoken by a character alone on stage to express private thoughts to the audience, while a monologue can be delivered even when other characters are present.
questions.p: Soliloquy na speech wey character dey talk when e dey alone for stage, to show im private mind to audience; monologue fit happen even if oda characters dey stage.

questions.q: Read this extract: 'Ngozi set down her basket. Suddenly, she was eight years old again, running barefoot through her grandmother's compound, the smell of fresh cocoyam stew filling the air.' Which narrative technique is shown here?
questions.e: The writer takes Ngozi (and the reader) back to an earlier time in her childhood; this technique of returning to a past event is called a flashback.
questions.p: Di writer carry Ngozi (and di reader) go back to one time wey happen before for her childhood; dis kain go-back-to-past-event na flashback.

questions.q: Which term describes a long narrative poem that celebrates the heroic deeds and adventures of a great legendary figure?
questions.e: An epic is a long narrative poem that tells the story of a hero's great deeds, often involving adventure, war or grand journeys.
questions.p: Epic na long poem wey dey tell story of one hero great work, e dey often involve adventure, war or big journey.

questions.q: In a story, the character who stands against the main character and causes conflict in the plot is called the...
questions.e: The antagonist is the character who opposes the protagonist (the main character), and this opposition creates the conflict that drives the story.
questions.p: Antagonist na di character wey dey stand against di protagonist (main character), and dis opposition na im dey cause di conflict wey dey push di story.

questions.q: Read this extract: 'Chief Okafor smiled warmly at the villagers who had gathered to celebrate the man they did not know he had secretly poisoned.' Which type of irony is illustrated here?
questions.e: The reader knows Chief Okafor poisoned the man, but the villagers celebrating do not know this; this gap between what the audience knows and what the characters know is dramatic irony.
questions.p: Reader know say Chief Okafor poison di man, but di villagers wey dey celebrate no know; dis kain gap wey dey between wetin audience know and wetin character know na dramatic irony.

questions.q: Which type of poem is written specifically to mourn and honour someone who has died?
questions.e: An elegy is a poem composed to mourn the death of a person and to honour their memory.
questions.p: Elegy na poem wey dem write to mourn person wey don die and to honour di person memory.

questions.q: Which of these best describes prose as a literary genre?
o: A short poem expressing personal feelings
Writing meant only to be performed before a live audience
Writing arranged in rhyming lines with a regular rhythm
Ordinary written or spoken language without a formal metrical structure
questions.e: Prose is ordinary written or spoken language, organised into sentences and paragraphs, without the formal metre or rhyme scheme found in poetry.
questions.p: Prose na normal written or spoken language, wey dem arrange for sentences and paragraphs, e no get di formal rhythm or rhyme wey poetry get.

questions.q: In a prose narrative, what is the term for the opening part of the story where the writer introduces the setting, main characters, and necessary background information?
questions.e: Exposition is the beginning part of a story that gives the setting, characters, and background needed to understand the plot. It comes before the rising action and climax.
questions.p: Exposition na the beginning part of story wey dey show the setting, characters and background wey go help person understand the story. E dey come before rising action and climax.

questions.q: A novel written in the first-person point of view is best described as one that is narrated by:
o: a character who refers to himself as 'I' and takes part in the action
a narrator who only reports what one character thinks, without using 'I'
a narrator who speaks directly to the reader as 'you' throughout
an all-knowing narrator who stands outside the story
questions.e: First-person narration means the story is told by a character inside the story who uses 'I' to describe events and his or her own experience. This is different from third-person narration where the narrator stays outside the action.
questions.p: First-person narration mean say na character wey dey inside the story dey tell am, e dey use 'I' to talk the events and wetin e experience. E different from third-person wey narrator dey outside the story.

questions.q: Read the passage: 'Chidi sat under the mango tree, staring blankly at his school certificate. Suddenly, his mind drifted back to the afternoon, ten years earlier, when his mother had sold her wrapper to pay his school fees.' Which narrative technique is used here?
questions.e: The passage moves from the present (Chidi under the mango tree) back to an earlier event (ten years before). This movement backward in time to an earlier event is called a flashback.
questions.p: The passage move from present time (Chidi under mango tree) go back to wetin happen ten years before. That kain movement go back for time na wetin dem dey call flashback.

questions.q: Read the passage: 'As Ngozi packed her bag for the journey, she paused and shivered, feeling that something terrible awaited her at the end of the road, though she could not explain why.' This sentence is best described as an example of:
questions.e: Ngozi's uneasy feeling hints at trouble that has not yet happened, preparing the reader for future events. This hinting at what will happen later in the story is called foreshadowing.
questions.p: Ngozi her uneasy feeling dey hint say trouble dey come, even though e never happen. This kain hint about wetin go happen later na foreshadowing.

questions.q: In Freytag's pyramid of plot structure, the point of greatest tension or turning point in a story, after which events begin to move toward the end, is called the:
questions.e: The climax is the highest point of tension or conflict in a story, the turning point after which the action begins to wind down toward the resolution.
questions.p: Climax na the highest point of tension or wahala for story, the turning point wey after am the story go begin move towards how e go end.

questions.q: A story that opens suddenly in the middle of an important action, with earlier events only explained later through narration or flashback, is said to begin:
questions.e: 'In medias res' is a Latin term meaning 'in the middle of things'. It describes a story that starts in the middle of the action rather than from the very beginning.
questions.p: 'In medias res' na Latin term wey mean 'for the middle of thing'. E dey describe story wey start for the middle of action instead of from the very beginning.

questions.q: Read the passage: 'Rain... the market... Mama's voice calling... no, that was years ago... the bus is late... will Baba forgive me... the smell of roasted corn...' Which narrative technique best describes this passage?
questions.e: The passage shows a character's thoughts jumping quickly between the present, memories, and random impressions without clear order. This free, unorganised flow of a character's thoughts is called stream of consciousness.
questions.p: The passage show how character thoughts dey jump quick-quick between present, memory, and random tins without order. This kain free flow of thought na stream of consciousness.

questions.q: Which of the following options correctly arranges the typical order of events in the traditional (Freytag) plot structure?
o: Climax, exposition, rising action, falling action, resolution
Exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution
Rising action, exposition, climax, resolution, falling action
Resolution, rising action, exposition, climax, falling action
questions.e: The standard plot structure begins with exposition (introduction), moves through rising action (building conflict), reaches the climax (turning point), then falling action, and ends with resolution. Option B follows this correct order.
questions.p: Normal plot structure dey start with exposition (introduction), e go through rising action (wahala dey build), reach climax (turning point), then falling action, e go end with resolution. Option B follow this correct order.

questions.q: Read the passage: 'I swear I never touched the money. Everyone in the village lied about me, even though I had counted the naira notes twice before hiding them under my mattress that same morning.' Based on this passage, the narrator can best be described as:
o: unreliable, because his own words contradict his claim of innocence
objective, because he reports only facts without feeling
omniscient, because he knows everyone's thoughts
reliable, because he speaks in the first person
questions.e: The narrator claims innocence, yet he admits to counting and hiding the money himself, which contradicts his claim. When a narrator's own words cannot be fully trusted because of such contradictions, he is called an unreliable narrator.
questions.p: The narrator talk say im no touch the money, but e confess say na im count and hide the money, wey contradict wetin e talk. When narrator word no fit trust because of this kain contradiction, dem dey call am unreliable narrator.

questions.q: A novel told entirely through letters exchanged between characters — for example, one where two friends, Bisi and Tolu, write to each other about their lives in Lagos and Kano — is known as what type of narrative?
questions.e: A novel told completely through letters, diary entries, or similar documents is called an epistolary novel. The example given, with Bisi and Tolu writing letters to each other, fits this definition exactly.
questions.p: Novel wey dem tell completely through letters, diary, or similar documents na epistolary novel. The example wey dem give, with Bisi and Tolu dey write letter to each other, match this definition well well.

questions.q: Which point of view uses pronouns like 'I' and 'we' to tell the story, as if the narrator is a character inside the events?
questions.e: A first person narrator uses 'I' or 'we' because the narrator is also a character who takes part in the story. The other points of view use 'he', 'she', 'they' or 'you'.
questions.p: First person narrator na im dey use 'I' or 'we' because di narrator sef be character wey dey inside di story. Di oda ones dey use 'he', 'she', 'they' or 'you'.

questions.q: A narrator who knows and can reveal the private thoughts and feelings of every character in a story is best described as a(n)...
questions.e: An omniscient narrator is like an all-knowing voice that can enter the minds of all the characters. This is different from a limited narrator, who can only access one character's thoughts.
questions.p: Omniscient narrator na di one wey sabi everytin, e fit enter di mind of all di characters. E different from limited narrator wey just sabi one character thoughts.

questions.q: Read this extract: 'I watched Mama count the naira notes under the lantern light, her lips moving silently as she calculated how far the money would stretch till the end of the month.' Which point of view is used here?
questions.e: The use of 'I' shows that the narrator is a character inside the story describing what he or she personally sees. This is a clear sign of first person narration.
questions.p: Di 'I' wey dem use show say na character wey dey inside di story dey talk wetin e see for im eye. Na so first person narration dey be.

questions.q: When a writer plainly tells the reader that a character is generous, instead of showing this through the character's actions or speech, the writer is using...
questions.e: Direct characterisation happens when the author openly states a character's trait, such as saying 'Chidi was a generous man'. Indirect characterisation, on the other hand, shows the trait through actions, speech or thoughts.
questions.p: Direct characterisation na when di writer just talk am straight say character get one quality, like 'Chidi na generous man'. Indirect characterisation na when dem show am through action or talk.

questions.q: In a prose work, the term 'setting' mainly refers to...
o: the time and place in which the story happens
the moral lesson taught by the story
the sequence of events in the plot
questions.e: Setting is the time and place of a story, including the historical period, season, and location. It is not the plot, theme, or conflict, though it can influence all of these.
questions.p: Setting na di time and place wia di story happen, e fit be di period, season or location. E no be di plot, theme or conflict, but e fit affect dem.

questions.q: A character who shows many different sides to his or her personality, and whose actions can sometimes surprise the reader, is called a...
questions.e: A round character is complex, has several traits, and can change or surprise the reader, unlike a flat character who has just one simple trait. Stock and static characters also remain predictable throughout the story.
questions.p: Round character na di one wey get plenty sides to im personality and fit surprise reader. Flat character get just one simple trait, while stock and static characters no dey change.

questions.q: Which statement best describes how setting can function in a prose work?
o: It helps to establish mood and can influence the actions of characters
It only decorates the story and has no real importance
It means the same thing as characterisation
It takes the place of the plot in a story
questions.e: Setting can create atmosphere or mood, such as fear or calmness, and can also shape how characters behave, for example poverty in a village pushing a character to steal. It is not the same as plot or characterisation.
questions.p: Setting fit bring mood or atmosphere, like fear or peace, and e fit affect how characters behave, like poverty wey make pesin steal. E no be di same as plot or characterisation.

questions.q: Read this extract: 'You stand at the edge of the market in Onitsha, the smell of dried fish and fresh pepper rushing into your nose as traders call out their prices.' Which point of view is this extract written in?
questions.e: The repeated use of 'you' directly addresses the reader as if the reader is the character experiencing the market. This unusual technique is called second person point of view, which is rarer than first or third person.
questions.p: Di 'you' wey dem use repeat show say dem dey talk to di reader like say na im be di character for market. Dis kain style na second person point of view, wey no too common pass first or third person.

questions.q: In a story, the character who stands against the main character and creates the major conflict is called the...
questions.e: The antagonist opposes the protagonist and is the source of conflict in the story. The protagonist is the main character, while a foil simply contrasts with another character to highlight traits.
questions.p: Antagonist na di one wey dey oppose di protagonist and dey cause di main conflict. Protagonist na di main character, while foil na pesin wey just dey contrast another character to show im qualities.

questions.q: In drama, a 'tragedy' is best described as a play that mainly presents:
o: A hero's serious downfall often caused by a flaw or fate, ending in suffering or death
A light story filled with jokes and happy endings
A mixture of serious and funny scenes with no clear ending
Exaggerated actions meant only to make the audience laugh
questions.e: Tragedy centres on a hero's serious downfall, often due to a tragic flaw, fate, or circumstances beyond control, usually ending in death or great suffering. The other options describe comedy or farce, not tragedy.
questions.p: Tragedy na play wey dey show how hero fall down well-well, sometimes because of im own mistake or because of fate, and e dey end for suffer or death. The other options na comedy or farce dem dey talk about.

questions.q: Which of these is a major feature that distinguishes comedy from tragedy in drama?
o: Comedy always involves kings and queens as main characters
Comedy ends happily and is meant to entertain and amuse the audience
Comedy must have five full acts like classical tragedy
Comedy always uses only prose, never verse
questions.e: Comedy is generally light-hearted, humorous, and ends on a happy note, unlike tragedy which ends in sorrow or death. The other options are not true requirements of comedy.
questions.p: Comedy na play wey dey light and funny, e dey end well-well make people laugh, no be like tragedy wey dey end for sorrow. Di order options no be real rule for comedy.

questions.q: A 'tragicomedy' in drama can be correctly described as a play that:
o: Has no plot at all, just random jokes
Must always be performed by children
Combines serious, sorrowful elements with comic or happy elements in one plot
Only makes the audience cry from beginning to end
questions.e: Tragicomedy blends the serious tone of tragedy with the light, happy tone of comedy, often moving from danger or sadness to a happy resolution. The other options do not reflect this mixed nature.
questions.p: Tragicomedy na play wey mix serious and sad matter with comedy and happy ending for one story. The other options no tally with wetin tragicomedy mean.

questions.q: Farce is a type of drama that is mainly known for:
o: Strict following of real-life events without exaggeration
Deep psychological study of a noble hero's suffering
Serious political speeches and long philosophical arguments
Exaggerated situations, physical comedy, and highly improbable events meant to cause laughter
questions.e: Farce relies on exaggerated, improbable situations, slapstick, and absurd misunderstandings purely to entertain and provoke laughter. It does not focus on deep tragedy or realistic, serious events.
questions.p: Farce na kain drama wey dey use too-much exaggeration, funny wahala and action wey no fit happen for real life just make people laugh. E no be about serious tragedy or real-life wahala.

questions.q: In a certain play, Chief Dapo Alade, a wealthy but proud businessman in Lagos, refuses to listen to warnings about a dangerous business deal. His pride leads to his downfall, loss of wealth, and eventually his death from shock. Which type of drama does this plot best represent?
questions.e: Chief Dapo's downfall is caused by his own pride (a tragic flaw), leading to suffering and death, which are the key features of tragedy. There is no comic relief or happy resolution to make it comedy or tragicomedy.
questions.p: Chief Dapo im pride na im bring im downfall, e suffer and die at the end, and dis one na wetin dey show inside tragedy. No comedy or happy ending dey make am comedy or tragicomedy.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes one key difference between comedy and farce?
o: Farce always ends in the death of the main character while comedy never does
Farce must contain a tragic hero while comedy must not
Comedy usually has believable characters and situations, while farce depends heavily on exaggeration and absurd coincidences
Comedy is only written in verse while farce is only written in prose
questions.e: Comedy, though humorous, usually keeps characters and events fairly believable, while farce exaggerates situations to an absurd, often unrealistic level purely for laughter. The other options are incorrect generalisations.
questions.p: Comedy dey use character and gist wey fit happen for real life, but farce dey blow matter big-big and unrealistic just to make people laugh. The other options no correct at all.

questions.q: A play shows a market woman, Mama Nkechi, who loses her entire goods to flood but later laughs with her neighbours as they help her start afresh, turning sorrow into hope by the final scene. Which dramatic type best fits this plot structure?
o: Pure comedy with no serious elements
questions.e: The play mixes a serious, sorrowful event (loss of goods) with a hopeful, community-supported resolution, which is the hallmark of tragicomedy. It is not pure tragedy because it ends in hope, and not pure comedy because it begins with real loss and sorrow.
questions.p: Di play mix serious sorrow (wen she lose her goods) with better ending (community help her), and dat one na tragicomedy style. E no be pure tragedy because di ending good, e no be pure comedy because sorrow dey inside too.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why classical tragedies often feature a hero of high social rank, such as a king or chief?
o: Because comedy does not allow for any character of high rank
So that the hero's downfall affects not just himself but also his family, followers, or kingdom, making the loss feel greater
To show that only poor people experience suffering
To make the play shorter and easier to stage
questions.e: A tragic hero of high status has far-reaching influence, so his fall creates wide-reaching consequences for his people, intensifying the tragic effect on the audience. The other options are not accurate explanations of this convention.
questions.p: When big person like king fall, e no just affect am alone, e dey affect im family, followers and even kingdom, so di tragedy go hit pass. Di other options no explain the reason well.

questions.q: In drama, 'comic relief' refers to:
o: The main plot of every farce
A long speech that ends a tragedy on a happy note
A rule that says comedies must always be shorter than tragedies
A funny scene or character inserted into a serious play to momentarily ease tension before the plot returns to seriousness
questions.e: Comic relief is a technique where a humorous moment is placed within a serious or tragic play to give the audience a short break from tension. It does not change the overall serious nature of the play.
questions.p: Comic relief na when dem put funny scene or character inside serious play make audience rest small before di serious matter continue. E no dey change di general serious tone of di play.

questions.q: A short scene shows two servants mistakenly swapping identical boxes meant for their masters, leading to a chain of ridiculous misunderstandings, slamming doors, and chasing around the stage, all resolved by sheer coincidence rather than careful planning. This scene is a clear example of:
questions.e: The exaggerated confusion, physical chasing, slamming doors, and resolution by mere coincidence rather than logical plot development are classic features of farce. There is no serious tragic element or realistic plausibility here to suggest the other options.
questions.p: Di mistake, di dey-run-up-and-down, di door wey dey bang, and how everything settle by luck instead of plan na clear sign of farce. No serious or real-life matter dey inside to call am tragedy or realistic drama.

questions.q: In drama, when a character speaks alone on stage, revealing his private thoughts and feelings to the audience without any other character hearing him, this technique is called:
questions.e: A soliloquy is a speech given by a character alone on stage, sharing his inner thoughts directly with the audience. No other character is present or aware of it.
questions.p: Soliloquy na when character dey alone for stage, e dey talk im mind give audience. No other character dey hear am.

questions.q: During a quarrel between two market women in a play, one of them turns briefly to the audience and whispers, 'This woman no sabi say na me go win dis case,' while the other woman continues talking, unaware of the comment. This short remark made to the audience, unheard by other characters on stage, is an example of:
questions.e: An aside is a brief remark a character makes directly to the audience, which other characters on stage are not supposed to hear. Here, the woman speaks to the audience while her rival continues unaware.
questions.p: Aside na short tin wey character talk give audience, wey the other characters no go hear. Na so the woman take talk am while her mate continue dey yarn, no sabi.

questions.q: A playwright creates two characters: Dapo, who is calm, patient, and always thinks before he acts, and his younger brother Wale, who is hot-tempered, impulsive, and quick to fight. Wale's reckless behaviour makes Dapo's calmness stand out more clearly to the audience. Wale, in this case, serves as Dapo's:
questions.e: A foil is a character whose qualities contrast with another character, making the other's traits more noticeable. Wale's impulsiveness highlights Dapo's calm nature by contrast.
questions.p: Foil na character wey im character dey different from another one, make dat other one character show well well. Wale im anger dey make Dapo im patience show clear.

questions.q: Which of these options correctly describes the main difference between a soliloquy and an aside?
o: A soliloquy is written in prose, while an aside is always written in verse
A soliloquy is a long, private speech delivered when a character believes he is alone, while an aside is a brief comment made to the audience even when other characters are present
A soliloquy is only used in comedies, while an aside is only used in tragedies
A soliloquy is spoken by two characters together, while an aside is spoken by one character alone
questions.e: A soliloquy is usually longer and spoken when the character is alone, revealing deep thoughts. An aside is shorter and can be spoken even when other characters are on stage, since only the audience hears it.
questions.p: Soliloquy long pass, na when character dey alone e dey yan im mind. Aside short, e fit happen even if other characters dey stage, but na only audience go hear am.

questions.q: In a short play, a security guard boasts to his colleague, 'No thief fit pass this gate while I dey on duty,' moments before a thief successfully sneaks past him unnoticed. This contrast between the guard's confident words and the actual outcome is an example of:
questions.e: Situational irony happens when the actual result is the opposite of what was expected. The guard expects no thief to pass, yet a thief passes, which is the opposite of his confident claim.
questions.p: Situational irony na when wetin happen no match wetin person expect. The guard talk say no thief go pass, but thief pass — na the opposite of wetin e talk.

questions.q: A character in a tragedy says to his friend, 'I am the happiest man alive today,' while the audience already knows his wife has just died in an accident he does not yet know about. This is an example of:
questions.e: This is dramatic irony because the audience possesses knowledge (the wife's death) that the character does not have, creating a painful contrast with his happy statement.
questions.p: Na dramatic irony be dis because audience sabi say im wife don die, but the man himself no sabi, so wetin e talk dey clash with wetin audience sabi.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why playwrights use the soliloquy technique in a drama?
o: To allow two characters to argue loudly on stage
To give the audience direct access to a character's private thoughts, motives, or plans without other characters' interference
To show stage directions clearly to the actors
To create background music for a scene
questions.e: Playwrights use soliloquy so that the audience can understand a character's inner mind, including secret plans, doubts, or motives, without any other character hearing it.
questions.p: Playwright dey use soliloquy make audience sabi wetin dey inside character mind, like im plan or wahala, without any other character dey hear am.

questions.q: In a play, a wealthy but foolish landlord named Chief Bassey always makes hasty decisions that cause trouble in his estate. His clerk, Mr. Eze, is wise, careful, and always advises caution before every action. Chief Bassey never listens, and the contrast between both men highlights Bassey's foolishness even more to the audience. What dramatic technique is most clearly at work here?
questions.e: Mr. Eze functions as a foil because his wisdom and caution are placed beside Chief Bassey's foolishness, making the landlord's bad judgement stand out sharply to the audience through contrast.
questions.p: Mr. Eze na foil character because im wisdom dey beside Chief Bassey im foolishness, so e dey make the landlord im bad decision show clear pass to audience.

questions.q: In a play, a king privately confides to the audience alone on stage: 'If I kill my brother tonight, the throne will finally be mine, but my conscience may never rest.' Later, during a public feast, he turns briefly aside to whisper to the audience, 'Watch how I will smile at him while my plan unfolds,' before continuing to laugh loudly with his brother in full view of the other guests. Which statement best explains the combined effect of these two techniques on the audience's understanding of the scene?
o: They reveal the king's true murderous plan privately, so his public friendliness towards his brother becomes deeply ironic to the audience
They prove that the brother already knows about the plan and is only pretending not to notice
They confuse the audience about the king's true intentions since he appears friendly throughout
They show that the king has genuinely forgiven his brother and abandoned his earlier plan
questions.e: The soliloquy and aside reveal the king's hidden murderous intention directly to the audience. This creates dramatic irony during the feast, since the audience knows the truth behind his false, friendly smiles while the brother and guests do not.
questions.p: Di soliloquy and aside show audience wetin dey inside king mind, say im wan kill im brother. So wen e dey smile for feast, na dramatic irony, because audience sabi the truth wey the brother no sabi.

questions.q: Which poetic form is traditionally made up of fourteen lines, usually written in iambic pentameter, and often deals with themes of love or deep personal feeling?
questions.e: A sonnet is a fixed poetic form of exactly fourteen lines, commonly in iambic pentameter. Odes, ballads and epics do not have this fixed fourteen-line structure.
questions.p: Sonnet na poem wey get fourteen lines, wey dem dey write for iambic pentameter, e dey talk about love or deep feelings. Ode, ballad and epic no get dat kain fourteen-line fixed style.

questions.q: Which poetic form is traditionally written to mourn and pay tribute to someone who has died, often reflecting on loss and grief?
questions.e: An elegy is a poem of mourning, written to lament the dead and reflect on loss. Ode celebrates, ballad tells a story, and epic recounts heroic deeds.
questions.p: Elegy na poem wey dem dey write to mourn person wey don die, e dey show sorrow and loss. Ode na praise poem, ballad na story poem, epic na hero poem.

questions.q: Which poetic form is a long narrative poem that celebrates the heroic deeds of a legendary or historical figure, often involving gods, long journeys and great battles?
questions.e: An epic is a long narrative poem about heroic deeds, often featuring gods and grand adventures, such as journeys and wars. Sonnets, elegies and odes are usually much shorter and do not focus on long heroic narratives.
questions.p: Epic na long story poem wey dey talk about hero wey do big things, sometimes with gods and big war or journey. Sonnet, elegy and ode dey short and no be about long hero story.

questions.q: Which statement best captures the main feature of an ode as a poetic form?
o: It must have a fixed structure of exactly fourteen lines
It tells a story in simple language, often with dialogue and a refrain
It has a dignified, elevated tone that praises or celebrates a person, object or idea
It has a solemn tone that mourns someone who has died
questions.e: An ode is known for its dignified and elevated tone used to praise or celebrate someone or something, like a river, a hero, or an idea. The other options describe an elegy, a sonnet and a ballad.
questions.p: Ode na poem wey get big, respectful tone wey dey praise person or thing. Di other options na for elegy, sonnet and ballad.

questions.q:
Read the extract below and answer the question that follows:

"The moon rose over Kaduna town,
A soldier marched with gun held tight,
His mother wept and called him down,
But he was gone into the night."

Which poetic form does this extract best represent?
questions.e: The extract tells a short story in simple quatrain form with alternating rhyme (town/down, tight/night), which is typical of a ballad. It is too short to be an epic and does not have the praise tone of an ode or the fourteen-line structure of a sonnet.
questions.p: Di extract dey tell short story for simple four-line stanza wey rhyme dey alternate (town/down, tight/night), na so ballad be. E too short to be epic, e no get praise tone like ode, e no also get fourteen lines like sonnet.

questions.q: A particular type of sonnet follows the rhyme scheme ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, made up of three quatrains followed by a rhyming couplet that usually delivers a twist, summary, or conclusion. This type of sonnet is known as the...
questions.e: The Shakespearean (English) sonnet has three quatrains and a final rhyming couplet, following the pattern ABAB CDCD EFEF GG. The Petrarchan sonnet instead divides into an octave and a sestet, usually without a closing couplet of this kind.
questions.p: Shakespearean sonnet get three quatrains plus one rhyming couplet for di end, di pattern be ABAB CDCD EFEF GG. Petrarchan sonnet dey different, e get octave and sestet, e no close with dat kain couplet.

questions.q:
Read the extract below and answer the question that follows:

"O mighty river, giver of life and yam,
Flow on forever, blessed be your name,
Your waters feed our farms from dawn to dusk,
We sing your praise, O river, without husk."

This extract is best classified as an example of which poetic form?
questions.e: The extract directly addresses the river in an elevated, celebratory tone, praising it for its life-giving power, which is the key feature of an ode. It is not mourning a death (elegy), telling a simple story (ballad), or recounting heroic deeds (epic).
questions.p: Di extract dey talk directly to di river for big, praise-praise tone, e dey celebrate di river because e dey give life, na so ode be. E no be about death (elegy), e no be simple story (ballad), e no also be about hero wahala (epic).

questions.q: Which of the following features is commonly found at the opening of a traditional epic poem?
o: A dialogue between two mourners expressing grief
A rhyming couplet that summarises the poem's moral lesson
A refrain that is repeated after every stanza
An invocation in which the poet calls on a muse or divine power for inspiration
questions.e: Traditional epics often open with an invocation, where the poet asks a muse or divine power for inspiration to tell the heroic story. Refrains are typical of ballads, rhyming couplets of sonnets, and mourning dialogue of elegies.
questions.p: Traditional epic dey normally start with invocation, where di poet dey call muse or divine power make e helep am tell di hero story. Refrain na for ballad, rhyming couplet na for sonnet, and mourning dialogue na for elegy.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches a poetic form with its typical subject matter or purpose?
o: Ode - lament for someone who has died
Elegy - celebration of a wedding ceremony
Ballad - a story told in simple song-like verse
Sonnet - a long heroic narrative involving gods
questions.e: A ballad is a story told in simple, song-like verse, which correctly matches its purpose. Elegy is for mourning (not weddings), ode is for praise (not lament), and sonnet is short, not a long heroic narrative like an epic.
questions.p: Ballad na story wey dem dey tell for simple song-like verse, so e match well well. Elegy na for mourning (no be wedding), ode na for praise (no be lament), and sonnet dey short, e no be long hero story like epic.

questions.q: In poetry, alliteration is best described as...
o: the repetition of consonant sounds at the beginning of two or more neighbouring words
the matching of sounds at the end of lines of verse
the repetition of vowel sounds within non-rhyming words
the regular pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in a line
questions.e: Alliteration is the repeating of the same consonant sound at the start of words that are close together, for example 'big black bag'. The other options describe assonance, rhyme and rhythm instead.
questions.p: Alliteration na when same consonant sound dey repeat for the front of words wey near each other, like 'big black bag'. The other options na for assonance, rhyme and rhythm, no be alliteration.

questions.q: Read this line: 'The bright kite flies high in the quiet sky.' Which sound device is most clearly shown by the repeated long 'i' sound in 'bright', 'kite', 'high', 'quiet' and 'sky'?
questions.e: Assonance is the repetition of vowel sounds within words that are near each other. Here the long 'i' sound repeats in several words, not just at the beginning, so it is assonance, not alliteration or rhyme.
questions.p: Assonance na when vowel sound repeat inside words wey close to each other. Here the long 'i' sound dey repeat for many words, e no be only for beginning, so na assonance, no be alliteration or rhyme.

questions.q:
Read the stanza below:
'The rain falls down upon the land,
It wets the fields and wets the sand,
The farmers smile and shake each hand,
And thank the skies as they had planned.'
What is the rhyme scheme of this stanza?
questions.e: All four end words — land, sand, hand, planned — rhyme with one another, so every line shares the same rhyme sound. This is marked AAAA, also called a monorhyme.
questions.p: All the four end words — land, sand, hand, planned — dey rhyme together, so every line get the same rhyme sound. Dem go mark am as AAAA, wey be monorhyme.

questions.q: Which sound device is most evident in the sentence: 'Sola sells sweet soup by the stream every Saturday'?
questions.e: The repeated 's' sound at the start of 'Sola', 'sells', 'sweet', 'soup', 'stream' and 'Saturday' is alliteration. There is no end rhyme or special vowel pattern being emphasised here.
questions.p: The 's' sound wey dey repeat for front of 'Sola', 'sells', 'sweet', 'soup', 'stream' and 'Saturday' na alliteration. No end rhyme or special vowel pattern dey here.

questions.q:
Read the stanza:
'The market women call with cheer,
Their baskets full of yam and rice,
The children gather, drawing near,
To taste the bread that smells so nice.'
What is the rhyme scheme of this stanza?
questions.e: Line 1 ends in 'cheer' and line 3 ends in 'near', which rhyme (A); line 2 ends in 'rice' and line 4 ends in 'nice', which also rhyme (B). This alternating pattern gives ABAB.
questions.p: Line 1 wey end for 'cheer' and line 3 wey end for 'near' dey rhyme (A); line 2 wey end for 'rice' and line 4 wey end for 'nice' dey rhyme too (B). Na so the pattern take be ABAB.

questions.q: Which of the following lines best illustrates assonance?
o: Deep green trees sleep in the cool evening breeze.
Peter picked plenty pepper for the pepper soup.
The sun rose over the misty hill, and the birds began to trill.
Ngozi walked quietly along the narrow path.
questions.e: In 'Deep green trees sleep in the cool evening breeze', the long 'ee' vowel sound repeats inside several words (deep, green, sleep, breeze), which is assonance. Option B is alliteration and option C is end rhyme, not assonance.
questions.p: For 'Deep green trees sleep in the cool evening breeze', the long 'ee' vowel sound dey repeat inside plenty words (deep, green, sleep, breeze), na assonance be that. Option B na alliteration and option C na end rhyme, no be assonance.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'rhythm' as used in poetry?
o: the arrangement of lines into a fixed number of stanzas
the repetition of the same consonant sound at the end of words
the pattern created by the alternation of stressed and unstressed syllables in a line
the use of a word that imitates the sound it describes
questions.e: Rhythm refers to the musical flow of a poem created by how stressed and unstressed syllables alternate. The other options describe consonance, onomatopoeia and stanza arrangement, which are different concepts.
questions.p: Rhythm na the musical flow wey poem get because of how stressed and unstressed syllables dey alternate. The other options dey talk about consonance, onomatopoeia and stanza arrangement, wey no be rhythm.

questions.q: Read the line: 'The boy ran fast to catch the early bus.' When scanned, the stresses fall as: 'the BOY ran FAST to CATCH the EAR-ly BUS.' Which term best describes this rhythmic pattern, where an unstressed syllable is regularly followed by a stressed syllable?
questions.e: A pattern of unstressed syllable followed by a stressed syllable (te-TUM) is called iambic rhythm. Trochaic rhythm is the reverse (stressed then unstressed), and free verse and monorhyme are unrelated terms.
questions.p: When unstressed syllable dey follow by stressed syllable (te-TUM), dem dey call am iambic rhythm. Trochaic rhythm na the opposite one (stressed before unstressed), while free verse and monorhyme no concern rhythm pattern like this.

questions.q:
Read the stanza:
'The river flows beneath the bridge so old,
It carries tales that have never been told,
The fishermen cast their nets with care,
Hoping for a catch beyond compare.'
What is the rhyme scheme of this stanza, and what name is given to two consecutive rhyming lines like 'old' and 'told'?
o: ABBA; this pairing is called a tercet
AABB; this pairing is called a couplet
ABAB; this pairing is called a quatrain
AAAA; this pairing is called a refrain
questions.e: Lines 1 and 2 rhyme (old/told) and lines 3 and 4 rhyme (care/compare), giving the pattern AABB. Two consecutive rhyming lines like this are called a couplet, not a quatrain, tercet or refrain.
questions.p: Line 1 and 2 dey rhyme (old/told) and line 3 and 4 dey rhyme (care/compare), so e be AABB. Two lines wey rhyme like that, one after the other, na couplet, e no be quatrain, tercet or refrain.

questions.q: A fourteen-line poem follows the rhyme scheme ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, ending with a rhyming couplet. This rhyme pattern is most closely associated with which poetic form?
questions.e: The ABAB CDCD EFEF GG pattern across fourteen lines, closing with a couplet, is the classic structure of the Shakespearean (English) sonnet. The Petrarchan sonnet instead uses an octave and sestet pattern, while ballads and free verse do not follow this scheme.
questions.p: The ABAB CDCD EFEF GG pattern for fourteen lines, wey end with couplet, na the classic structure of Shakespearean (English) sonnet. Petrarchan sonnet dey use octave and sestet pattern instead, while ballad and free verse no follow this kind scheme.

questions.q: "Adaeze's smile was as warm as the afternoon sun." Which figure of speech is used in this sentence?
questions.e: The sentence compares Adaeze's smile to the sun using the word 'as', which is the mark of a simile. A metaphor would make the comparison without 'like' or 'as'.
questions.p: Dis sentence dey compare Adaeze smile to sun with di word 'as', na so simile dey work. Metaphor no go use 'like' or 'as'.

questions.q: "During break time, the classroom became a market square." This sentence contains which figure of speech?
questions.e: The classroom is directly called a 'market square' without using 'like' or 'as', so this is a metaphor. It is a direct comparison, not a literal statement.
questions.p: Dem call di classroom 'market square' straight, no 'like' or 'as' dey inside, so na metaphor. E be direct comparison.

questions.q: "The old wooden bridge groaned and complained as the lorry crossed it." Which figure of speech is at work here?
questions.e: The bridge, which is a non-living object, is given human actions of groaning and complaining. Giving human qualities to non-human things is called personification.
questions.p: Dem give di bridge, wey no be living thing, human action like to groan and complain. To give human quality to non-human thing na personification.

questions.q: "Seven slippery snakes slithered silently across the swamp." Which figure of speech is most clearly shown in this sentence?
questions.e: Most of the words begin with the same consonant sound 's', which is repeated close together. This repetition of initial consonant sounds is called alliteration.
questions.p: Plenty of di words dey begin with di same 's' sound wey dey repeat close-close. Dis kain repeat of first consonant sound na alliteration.

questions.q: Mr. Bello told his students, "I have warned you a thousand times not to shout in my class!" What figure of speech did he use?
questions.e: Mr. Bello did not literally warn his students a thousand times; he exaggerated to show how often he has warned them. Deliberate exaggeration for emphasis is called hyperbole.
questions.p: Mr. Bello no really warn dem one thousand times, na exaggeration e use to show say e don warn dem plenty times. Dis kain exaggeration wey dem use for emphasis na hyperbole.

questions.q: "The old gate banged shut with a loud clang as the wind blew through the compound." Which word in this sentence best illustrates onomatopoeia?
questions.e: The word 'banged' imitates the actual sound a gate makes when it closes forcefully. Onomatopoeia is a word that imitates the sound it describes.
questions.p: Di word 'banged' dey copy di real sound wey gate dey make when e close hard-hard. Onomatopoeia na word wey dey copy di sound wey e dey describe.

questions.q: A fire outbreak destroyed the town's fire service headquarters, the very building meant to prevent fire disasters. What figure of speech best describes this situation?
questions.e: The outcome is the opposite of what is expected, since the fire station, built to fight fires, is destroyed by fire itself. This unexpected contrast between expectation and reality is situational irony.
questions.p: Di result be di opposite of wetin pesin go expect, becos di fire station, wey dem build to fight fire, na fire burn am. Dis kain surprise contrast na situational irony.

questions.q: "A deafening silence filled the hall as the results were about to be announced." Which figure of speech is used in this sentence?
questions.e: 'Deafening' and 'silence' are two contradictory words placed together, since silence cannot truly be deafening. Combining opposite or contradictory terms for effect is called an oxymoron.
questions.p: 'Deafening' and 'silence' na two words wey no match, becos silence no fit really deafen pesin. To combine opposite words like dis na oxymoron.

questions.q: "The Palace has refused to comment on the chieftaincy dispute in the town." In this sentence, the word 'Palace' is used to represent which of the following?
o: A metonymy for the monarchy or royal authority
questions.e: 'Palace' is used to stand for the monarchy or the royal authority that occupies it, not the building itself. Using a closely associated word to represent something is called metonymy.
questions.p: Dem dey use 'Palace' to represent di monarchy or royal authority wey dey inside am, no be di building. To use word wey close to something to represent am na metonymy.

questions.q: "O Sleep, why do you refuse to visit my tired eyes tonight?" Which figure of speech is used in this line?
questions.e: The speaker directly addresses 'Sleep', which is an abstract idea that cannot hear or respond, as though it were a person present. Directly addressing an absent or non-human thing is called apostrophe.
questions.p: Di speaker dey talk direct to 'Sleep', wey be abstract tin wey no fit hear or answer, as if e be person wey dey there. To address absent or non-human tin like dis na apostrophe.

questions.q:
Read the following extract carefully and answer the question that follows:

"The sun had barely lifted its head above the iroko trees when Mama Ngozi began her journey to Oye market. Her basket, heavy with yams and bitter leaf, pressed into her shoulder like an old debt that refused to be forgotten. She walked without looking back, for she knew that behind her lay a compound of hungry mouths waiting for the coins she would bring home. By the time she reached the market gate, her wrapper was soaked with sweat, yet her eyes still shone with the stubborn hope of a woman who had buried two husbands and raised five children alone."

Which point of view does the narrator use to tell this story?
o: First person narrator, a character in the story
Second person narrator addressing the reader directly
questions.e: The narrator is not a character in the story but knows Mama Ngozi's private thoughts, feelings and past life (that she buried two husbands and raised five children). This all-knowing outside view is third person omniscient.
questions.p: Di one wey dey tell di story no be character inside di story, but e sabi Mama Ngozi mind and her past wella (like say she bury two husband). Na dat kind all-knowing style be third person omniscient.

questions.q:
Read the following extract carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Chidi stood at the riverbank, his fishing net trailing in the water like a tired old man's hand. Each evening for thirty years, he had come to this same spot, and each evening the river had given him just enough to keep hunger at bay but never enough to make him proud. Tonight, however, something tugged hard at the net, and his heart leapt like a drum struck by an eager hand. 'Could this be the day?' he whispered to the darkening sky, his voice trembling between fear and joy."

Where is this extract set?
o: At a busy market in the morning
By a riverbank in the evening
In a courtroom during a trial
questions.e: The extract clearly states Chidi 'stood at the riverbank' and mentions 'each evening', showing the setting is by a river in the evening.
questions.p: Di extract talk say Chidi 'stood at di riverbank' and e mention 'each evening', so di setting na riverside for evening time.

questions.q:
Read the lines below and answer the question that follows:

"The old man's beard was white as cotton wool,
And his eyes shone like dying embers."

What figure of speech is used in BOTH lines?
questions.e: Both lines use 'as' and 'like' to directly compare two unlike things (beard to cotton wool, eyes to embers). This direct comparison using 'like' or 'as' is called a simile.
questions.p: Both lines use 'as' and 'like' to compare two different things wey no resemble (beard to cotton wool, eye to embers). When you compare like that with 'like' or 'as', na simile be that.

questions.q:
Study this stanza:

"The farmer tills his land at dawn,
His hands are rough, his shirt is worn,
He sings a song of hope and rain,
To ease his heart and ease his pain."

What is the rhyme scheme of the stanza?
questions.e: The end words are dawn/worn (rhyme pair 1) and rain/pain (rhyme pair 2). This gives the pattern AABB, where the first two lines rhyme and the last two lines rhyme.
questions.p: The last words be dawn/worn (dem rhyme together) and rain/pain (dem rhyme together too). So the pattern na AABB - first two lines rhyme, last two lines rhyme.

questions.q:
"Mama's hands are rivers of patience, flowing gently over every mistake."

What figure of speech is used in this sentence?
questions.e: The sentence says Mama's hands ARE rivers, without using 'like' or 'as'. This direct, implied comparison between two unlike things is a metaphor, not a simile.
questions.p: E say Mama hands na rivers, e no use 'like' or 'as'. Dis kind direct comparison wey no get 'like' or 'as' na metaphor, e no be simile.

questions.q:
"The thunder clapped its hands in anger, and the storm clouds wept bitterly all night."

Which literary device is most clearly demonstrated here?
questions.e: Thunder and clouds are given human actions and feelings - clapping hands and weeping - which only living beings can do. Giving human qualities to non-human things is personification.
questions.p: Thunder and cloud dey do human things - dem dey clap hand and dey cry. When you give human qualities to things wey no be human, na personification be that.

questions.q:
"Silent streams slide slowly south, soaking the sun-baked sand."

Which sound device dominates this line?
questions.e: The repeated consonant sound 's' at the beginning of several words (silent, streams, slide, slowly, south, soaking, sun, sand) is alliteration. Assonance deals with vowel sounds, not consonants.
questions.p: The 's' sound dey repeat for the start of plenty words (silent, streams, slide, slowly, south, soaking, sun, sand). Na alliteration be dat - assonance na for vowel sounds, no be consonant.

questions.q:
Read this extract:

"The children's ribs show through their skin,
Their eyes are hollow, void of play,
Mother searches bins for scraps of bread,
While hunger steals the light of day."

What is the dominant TONE of this extract?
questions.e: The images of hollow eyes, searching for scraps, and hunger stealing light all create a sad, pitiful feeling. This sorrowful attitude of the poet toward the subject is called a mournful tone.
questions.p: The pictures of hollow eye, searching for scrap food, and hunger wey dey steal light all dey show sorrow and pity. Dis kind sad feeling wey the poet get for the subject na mournful tone.

questions.q:
Consider this short poem:

"Harmattan wind blows
Dust settles on red rooftops
Dry season has come"

Counting the syllables in each line (5, 7, 5), what poetic form is this?
questions.e: A haiku is a three-line Japanese poetic form with a 5-7-5 syllable pattern, usually about nature or seasons. This poem matches that exact structure and theme.
questions.p: Haiku na three-line poem wey come from Japan, e get 5-7-5 syllable pattern and e dey always talk about nature or season. Dis poem match the structure and the topic well well.

questions.q:
"A deafening silence filled the courtroom as the judge rose to speak."

Which figure of speech is used in this sentence?
questions.e: 'Deafening' means very loud, while 'silence' means no sound at all - these are two contradictory ideas joined together. When opposite terms are combined for effect, it is called an oxymoron.
questions.p: 'Deafening' mean say e loud well well, but 'silence' mean say no sound dey at all - na two opposite ideas wey dem join together. When you combine opposite words like dat, na oxymoron.

questions.q:
"The aroma of jollof rice filled the compound, mingling with the sound of laughter and the sight of children dancing under the moonlight."

Which literary term best describes the use of smell, sound and sight in this sentence?
questions.e: The sentence appeals to the senses of smell (aroma), hearing (laughter) and sight (children dancing). Descriptive language that appeals to the five senses is called imagery.
questions.p: The sentence dey touch smell (aroma), hearing (laughter) and sight (pikin dey dance). Any kind description wey dey touch our five senses like dis na imagery.

questions.q: In literary studies, what does the term 'tone' mean?
o: The order in which events happen in the plot
The physical setting where the story takes place
The main message the writer wants readers to learn
The writer's attitude towards the subject matter or the audience
questions.e: Tone refers to the writer's or speaker's attitude towards the subject or the reader. It can be serious, playful, sarcastic, sad, and so on. It is different from setting, plot or theme.
questions.p: Tone na how the writer or speaker feel about the matter wey e dey talk about, e fit be vex tone, happy tone, mock tone. E no be where story happen or how story arrange.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'mood' in a literary work?
o: The central idea or message a writer wants to pass across
The sequence of events arranged by the writer
The atmosphere or feeling that a piece of writing creates in the reader
The full list of characters that appear in a play
questions.e: Mood is the overall feeling or atmosphere a reader experiences while reading a text, such as fear, joy or sadness. It is created through word choice, setting and imagery.
questions.p: Mood na the kain feeling wey the story give the person wey dey read am, e fit be fear, happiness or sadness. Na the words and the picture wey the writer paint dey cause am.

questions.q: Read this extract: 'The old hut stood alone on the hill, its roof sagging like the shoulders of a tired old man, windows staring like empty eyes into the grey evening.' What mood does this extract create?
questions.e: Words like 'alone', 'sagging', 'tired', 'empty eyes' and 'grey evening' build a lonely, gloomy and frightening atmosphere. This shows an eerie and desolate mood, not a happy or funny one.
questions.p: The kain words wey dem use like 'alone', 'tired', 'empty eyes' and 'grey evening' dey show one fearful, lonely feeling. So the mood na eerie and desolate, e no be happy or funny one.

questions.q: A father says to his son, 'Oh wonderful! You have failed your exams again, just what this family needed.' What tone is the father expressing?
questions.e: The father does not really mean 'wonderful'; he is using the opposite of what he feels to mock the situation. This is sarcasm, a tone used to express the opposite meaning for mocking effect.
questions.p: The papa no mean say na correct thing, im dey use 'wonderful' to mock the pikin wey fail exam. Na sarcasm, where person talk the opposite of wetin im mean to mock person.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the 'theme' of a literary work?
o: The list of literary devices the writer uses
The historical period during which the work was written
The particular event or topic the writer chooses to describe
The central message or underlying idea the writer communicates through the work
questions.e: Theme is the central or underlying idea, lesson or message that runs through a literary work, such as love, betrayal or greed. It is more abstract than the actual story being told.
questions.p: Theme na the main message or lesson wey dey inside the story, like love, betrayal or greed. E dey different from the actual story wey dem tell, because theme na the deep idea.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly explains the difference between 'subject matter' and 'theme' in a literary work?
o: Subject matter and theme always mean the exact same thing in every text
Subject matter is the actual topic or story being presented while theme is the underlying message or idea behind it
Subject matter is the writer's attitude to the reader while theme is the setting of the story
Subject matter is the moral lesson while theme is just a summary of the plot
questions.e: Subject matter is what the work is actually about on the surface, such as a war or a wedding, while theme is the deeper message the writer wants to pass across using that subject matter.
questions.p: Subject matter na the real topic wey the story dey talk about for surface, like war or wedding, but theme na the deep message wey the writer wan pass through that topic.

questions.q: Read this extract: 'Mama smiled and patted my head, but her eyes refused to meet mine, and her hand trembled slightly as she said, "Everything will be fine, my son."' What is the overall tone of this extract?
questions.e: Although Mama's words sound comforting, her trembling hand and avoiding eyes contradict her calm words, showing that she is actually worried. The true tone is anxiety hidden under a forced calm, not real confidence.
questions.p: Even though Mama talk say everything go fine, her shaking hand and the way she no fit look the pikin for eye show say she dey fear. So the real tone na worry wey she dey hide under fake calmness, e no be real confidence.

questions.q: Read this extract: 'The market square buzzed with laughter, drums rolled, and children in colourful aso-ebi ran between the stalls chasing one another, while the aroma of roasted corn filled the air.' What mood does this passage create?
questions.e: Details like laughter, rolling drums, colourful clothes, playing children and the smell of roasted corn all point to a lively celebration. These images create a festive and joyful mood.
questions.p: The laughter, drum wey dey roll, fine clothes, pikin wey dey play and the smell of roasted corn dey show say na celebration dey happen. All these things na the festive and joyful mood.

questions.q: A short story tells of Chief Obi, who spent his whole life gathering wealth and refused to help his brothers even during their hardship. On his deathbed, surrounded by riches but with no family beside him, he wept alone. Which theme best fits this story?
o: The emptiness of greed and the importance of kinship
questions.e: Chief Obi's wealth could not bring him comfort or family love at the end of his life, showing that greed without care for relatives leads to loneliness. The theme is about the emptiness of greed and the value of family ties.
questions.p: Even though Chief Obi get plenty money, e no get family beside am when e dey die, because e be greedy person wey no help im brothers. The theme na say greed na empty thing and family relationship important pass money.

questions.q: A wife shouts at her husband, 'How dare you waste the little money we have on gambling, while your children go hungry!' What is the tone of the wife in this statement?
questions.e: The wife is scolding and blaming her husband strongly for his careless action, which shows a reproachful (rebuking) tone. She is clearly not indifferent, playful or showing admiration.
questions.p: The wife dey blame and scold her husband seriously because of the gambling wey e do while children dey hungry. That kain blaming attitude na reproachful tone, e no be indifferent, play-play or admiration.

questions.q: Read this line: 'Mr. Okafor's temper was like a thunderstorm that could strike without warning.' Which figure of speech is used here?
questions.e: The line compares Mr. Okafor's temper to a thunderstorm using the word 'like'. Any comparison using 'like' or 'as' is a simile.
questions.p: Di sentence compare Mr. Okafor im temper to thunderstorm, and e use 'like'. Any time wey comparison use 'like' or 'as', na simile be dat.

questions.q: In the sentence 'Hope danced joyfully in her eyes as she opened the result slip,' which literary device is used?
questions.e: Hope, which is a feeling and not a human being, is described as 'dancing', giving it a human action. Giving human qualities to non-human things is personification.
questions.p: Hope no be human being but di sentence talk say e dance. When you give non-human thing human action, na personification.

questions.q: Consider this line from a short poem: 'Ngozi's heart was a drum beating wildly through the examination hall.' What figure of speech has the poet used?
questions.e: The poet directly calls Ngozi's heart 'a drum' without using 'like' or 'as'. A direct comparison of two unlike things without 'like/as' is a metaphor.
questions.p: Di poet call Ngozi im heart 'a drum' straight, no 'like' or 'as' dey. Wen you compare two different tins straight like dat, na metaphor.

questions.q: In a stage play, a character stands alone on an empty stage and speaks his private thoughts aloud so the audience can understand his inner conflict. What is this dramatic technique called?
questions.e: A soliloquy is a speech a character gives while alone on stage, revealing private thoughts to the audience. An aside is a short comment to the audience while others are still present, and a monologue can be given even when other characters are on stage.
questions.p: Soliloquy na wen character dey alone for stage, e dey tok im mind give audience. Aside na small-small tok wen oda pipo still dey stage, monologue fit happun even if oda pipo dey stage.

questions.q: In a play, the audience sees a servant secretly pour poison into the king's wine, but the king does not know and happily raises his cup to toast his guests. What type of irony is this?
questions.e: The audience knows a fact (the poison) that the king, a character in the play, does not know. This gap in knowledge between the audience and a character is called dramatic irony.
questions.p: Audience sabi say poison dey di wine, but di king sef no sabi. Dis kain gap wey dey between wetin audience sabi and wetin character sabi na dramatic irony.

questions.q: Which term correctly describes the main character around whom the events of a story or play revolve?
questions.e: The protagonist is the central or leading character whose actions and conflicts drive the plot. The antagonist opposes the protagonist, while a foil only highlights another character's traits by contrast.
questions.p: Protagonist na di main character wey di whole story dey follow. Antagonist na di one wey dey fight against am, foil na character wey just dey show difference from anoda character.

questions.q: The phrase 'a deafening silence filled the courtroom after the judge's verdict' contains which literary device?
questions.e: 'Deafening' and 'silence' are two contradictory words placed side by side to create a striking effect; this short combination of opposite words is called an oxymoron. A paradox is usually a longer statement that seems self-contradictory but reveals a deeper truth.
questions.p: 'Deafening' and 'silence' na two wahala words wey no match but dem put dem togeda. Dis short combo of opposite words na oxymoron. Paradox na longer statement wey dey sound like contradiction but e get truth inside.

questions.q: In a tragedy, King Babatunde's excessive ambition eventually causes his own destruction, even though he starts the play as a respected and powerful ruler. What literary term best names this fatal character weakness that leads to his downfall?
questions.e: Hamartia is the general term for the fatal flaw or error of judgement in a tragic hero that leads to his downfall. Catharsis refers to the audience's emotional release, and peripeteia is the sudden reversal of fortune, not the flaw itself.
questions.p: Hamartia na di general word for di mistake or weakness wey dey cause tragic hero im downfall. Catharsis na di feeling wey audience get afta di play, peripeteia na di sudden change of fortune, no be di weakness.

questions.q: 'Mama mixed melon for the market' is an example of which sound device, since the 'm' sound is repeated at the beginning of several words?
questions.e: Alliteration is the repetition of the same consonant sound at the beginning of neighbouring or closely connected words, as seen with the repeated 'm' sound here. Assonance deals with repeated vowel sounds, not the beginning consonant sounds of words.
questions.p: Alliteration na wen one consonant sound repeat for front of words wey close to each oda, like dis 'm' sound here. Assonance na about vowel sound wey repeat, no be beginning consonant.

questions.q: At the end of a novel, all the conflicts are resolved: the lovers reunite, the villain is punished, and peace returns to the village. What is this final part of the plot called?
questions.e: The denouement is the final part of a story where all the loose ends and conflicts are resolved after the climax. The climax is the turning point of highest tension, while exposition and rising action occur earlier in the plot.
questions.p: Denouement na di last part of story wey dem solve all di wahala afta di climax. Climax na di point wey tension high pass, while exposition and rising action dey happun before di climax.
